messages:
Alex (customer): Hey, started getting 403s for SSO logins right after our IdP rotated signing certs an hour ago. No code changes on our side.
Maya (support): Thanks Alex — can you paste the auth failure log (request id) and the ACS URL you have configured in the SP?
Alex (customer): request_id=sp-9f2c3b; ACS we configured: https://app.customer-inc.com:8443/saml/acs (we added port last release).
Maya (support): Hmm port in ACS can be picky — our SAML recipient check is exact match. Two quick checks: 1) is the metadata the IdP publishes showing the new cert? 2) can our metadata fetcher reach the IdP URL now?
Alex (customer): IdP metadata shows new KeyDescriptor and signature, yes. But our security team says their corporate proxy is forcing gzip and a basic auth challenge for some calls. Not sure if that affects the fetch.
Jonas (infra): @Maya possible that the metadata fetch returned an intermediate 200 with chunked+gzip and our metadata watcher ignored the body -> stale cert in cache. I see a fetch attempt around 4312345600 that returned 502 from a proxy in logs. I'll pull proxy logs.
Sam (eng-oncall): Also double-check SP entityID vs ACS recipient. Some IdPs validate the recipient strictly and will reject if Host/Port or trailing slash differs. Can you try a direct curl from our fetcher region?
Maya (support): Alex, can you run this from an environment that reaches the IdP directly and paste output:
```
curl -v -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' 'https://idp.customer-inc.com/metadata' -o -
```
Alex (customer): Running now, output snippet: ``* Received HTTP/1.1 200 OK
* Content-Encoding: gzip
* Transfer-Encoding: chunked
* Content-Type: application/samlmetadata+xml; charset=utf-8
<binary gzipped blob>``
Alex (customer): After gunzip the XML, cert is present. No BOM. SignedMetadata element looks fine.
Maya (support): Ok good. @Jonas can you confirm our fetcher didn't retry/purge the cache after the 502? If cached old cert, we would still validate against previous key and fail.
Jonas (infra): Checking — fetcher logs show a fetch at 4312345598 that returned 502 (proxy auth), then a success at 4312345620 with 200 but Content-Encoding header present. Our parser code has a bug where it assumed content-length not chunked and threw on chunked+gzip in that path. The watchdog didn't replace the cached entry. Bug filed internally.
Sam (eng-oncall): That would explain the timing. Meanwhile you can work around this by either: 1) adding an alternate ACS entry without the :8443 port in your SP configuration, or 2) making the IdP publish an <AssertionConsumerService Location> matching the exact ACS with port. Which is easier for you?
Alex (customer): We can add alt ACS without port for testing. Quick question: if metadata is signed, do we need to update fingerprint somewhere?
Maya (support): If the IdP rotates signing certs but keeps the metadata URL signature updated, we will pick it up on successful fetch. If you're pinning a fingerprint in your SP config, you'll need to update that to the new cert's SHA256. Otherwise no change.
Alex (customer): Ok added duplicate ACS (no port). Testing now...
sso-bot: metadata-watcher: fetcher triggered for idp.customer-inc.com at 4312345710, status=200, parser=ok
Alex (customer): Good news — login works with the ACS without port. The app was failing when IdP validated recipient and saw port mismatch.
Maya (support): Great. Long term we'd prefer the IdP to publish an ACS that exactly matches the SP (including port) or for your SP entity to list both Locations. Also we'll push a fix for the chunked+gzip handling so cache updates aren't skipped.
Jonas (infra): Filed infra bug INF-2026: metadata parser rejects chunked+gzip in partial-read path. ETA for patch: 24h. I'll add a temporary aggressive refetch for this tenant.
Sam (eng-oncall): Action items: Maya — confirm workaround with Alex and remove after IdP adjusts metadata or we deploy patch. Jonas — patch/monitor. Alex — coordinate with IdP to publish exact ACS entry or allow the portless location.
Alex (customer): Thanks everyone. One more tiny repro note for your triage: the IdP responds with `Vary: Accept-Encoding` and `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Some intermediate proxies were adding auth challenges and returning 502 which caused the stale-cache window.
Maya (support): Helpful, thanks. Marking this thread for follow-up. If we roll the patch we'll post here. :thumbsup:
Alex (customer): Thanks all, saved my afternoon :)
Sam (eng-oncall): Will follow up once INF-2026 patch lands.
Maya (support): Closing here for now — reopen if you see regressions.
